records.supported_name_scope: Río Tamanaco is directly printed along the selected western south-running corridor and the east-running reach north of Tucupido. Embalse Playa de Piedra is a distinct selected reservoir passage. Río Unare is directly labeled on the receiving north-running lower river and near the coastal outlet. Laguna de Píritu names the eastern lagoon/marsh setting toward which the model ends; it is not a river alias.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins on the south-running Tamanaco corridor west of San José de Guaribe, descends through the San Antonio de Tamanaco vicinity and enters Embalse Playa de Piedra. Below the reservoir it turns east, passes north of Tucupido and continues through the lower Tamanaco bends to the Unare receiving corridor north of Zaraza. The selection then follows lower Unare past San José de Unare and Onoto, through the Guaribe receiving vicinity and past the Guanape approach near Clarines. In the coastal plain it follows the named Unare toward the land between Laguna de Unare and Laguna de Píritu, but its last straight segment leaves the mapped channel and runs northeast toward the western Píritu lagoon/marsh edge. The upper Unare arriving from Zaraza, Quebrada Honda, the separate Embalse de Tucupido, and the Guaribe and Guanape upstream branches are not substituted for the selection.
records.region: Northeastern Venezuela, from the Tamanaco mountain-front corridor in Guárico through the Tucupido and San José de Unare settings to the coastal plain west of Puerto Píritu in Anzoátegui.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity; not a uniform name for the selected Tamanaco, reservoir, Unare and unresolved lagoonward terminal route.
records.completion_scope: The complete selected extent was inspected on the retained original TPC K-27D government chart, with necessary upper, reservoir, middle, confluence, lower and coastal crops. A newly acquired original JOG NC 20-5 at twice the chart scale resolves the terminal geography and confirms that a continuous channel is not depicted along the final straight lagoonward segment. The representative Unare identity and bounded upstream component sequence are supported, but actual correspondence for that terminal connection is still missing. Complete visual coverage is not claimed as completed whole-route correspondence. Separate approximate orientation overlays were used only to locate the retained selection; original pixels supplied the labels and waterways.
records.material_pending_reason: A continuous actual channel along the final straight segment from lower Unare toward the western Laguna de Píritu edge is not established by either inspected original chart. The larger-scale JOG shows the named river bending north toward its separate coastal opening, while the retained diagonal crosses toward the eastern marsh/lagoon. A distinct permissible primary source resolving that selected connection is needed before claiming full-route correspondence. This is a route-material gap, not simply a missing hydronym.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Selected south-running Tamanaco reach below the mountain front; not an official source-point determination.
naming_scope_details.upper_named_component: Río Tamanaco above and below Embalse Playa de Piedra.
naming_scope_details.middle_component: Lower Río Tamanaco east of Tucupido and its receiving junction with Unare north of Zaraza.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Río Unare below the Tamanaco junction, through the San José de Unare, Onoto and Clarines corridor to the coastal plain.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Unresolved straight model segment leaving the mapped lower Unare toward the western Laguna de Píritu marsh/lagoon edge.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Río Unare uniformly to the Tamanaco reaches, Embalse Playa de Piedra, lagoonward diagonal or Laguna de Píritu.
Do not substitute the actual mapped Unare mouth at La Cerca for the retained lagoonward terminal segment and then claim whole-route correspondence.
Do not infer a channel name, canal, historical avulsion, present-day flow or cause of the terminal model/map difference.
The upper Unare from Zaraza, Quebrada Honda, Embalse de Tucupido, and upper Guaribe and Guanape approaches remain separate from the selected route.
No independent initial-feeder name, reservoir alias, legal naming date, Indigenous alternate or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 281.676 km is the retained modeled route length, not an official length of Río Unare or Río Tamanaco. The chart generalizes meanders, reservoir shores and marshes. The final straight lagoonward segment is not continuously supported by a mapped channel. No geometry modification, correction, precision registration or revalidation was performed.

records.supported_name_scope: Repeated readable Thomsen River labels identify the central northward valley and its large northwestward bend. The northern source shows the selected ending on the channel labeled Desert River west of Castel Bay, beside the separately labeled Nangmagvik Lake. The initial southern approach and the link between the Thomsen and Desert corridors are not assigned either name.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins on a short western stream-and-lake approach, runs south, makes a broad eastward elbow and returns north through the southern lake country. It reaches the labeled Thomsen corridor below the separate western upper-Thomsen lake approach, continues north past the southern park boundary and Green Cabin setting, bends northwest near White Sand Creek and proceeds north past the Able Creek and Muskox River settings. In the lower northern section the modeled line leaves the mapped Thomsen corridor to the northwest. Thomsen itself continues northeast into Castel Bay, while the selected tail reaches the separate north-running Desert River/Nangmagvik Lake corridor and its coastline west of the bay. Mercy Bay is farther east and is not the selected ending.
records.region: Central and northern Banks Island, Northwest Territories, Canada, including the Thomsen valley in Aulavik National Park and the separate Desert River coast west of Castel Bay.
records.completion_scope: Four original federal base-map views and the original Parks Canada river-guide map were acquired and inspected. Together they provide readable geographic coverage across the full selection, establish the two named component corridors, and expose unresolved actual route correspondence in the southern elbow and the northern transfer between separate river valleys. Full selected-route correspondence is therefore not completed. Missing connections are not treated as ordinary name gaps or harmless meander simplification.
records.material_pending_reason: Readable primary cartography does not establish the full southern headward elbow or a continuous Thomsen-to-Desert transfer along the retained selection. The central and terminal sections have distinct supported river identities. A single representative name and complete selected-route correspondence remain unresolved.

unresolved_components: The complete initial southward approach, southern eastward elbow and transition to the northern southern-lake-country corridor.
The northern transfer from the Thomsen valley toward the separate Desert River corridor.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Desert River coastal opening west of Castel Bay; no exact modern tidal limit or shoreline survey is claimed.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Thomsen River to the entire selected line or identify the modeled terminal as its Castel Bay mouth.
Do not treat Desert River as an alias, downstream name or established receiving continuation of Thomsen River.
Do not treat Nangmagvik Lake, Shoran Lake, Lemming Lake or Twin Lakes as uniformly traversed river reaches.
No name is forced onto the unresolved southern feeder, its small lakes or the northern connecting interval. No Indigenous alternative, formal naming date or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 281.277 km value is the retained modeled display length, not an official length of either named river. The retained line generalizes channels and lakes, but the identified southern and northern correspondence gaps go beyond a supported named-corridor simplification. No geometry modification or point-by-point geometry revalidation was performed.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Four original federal base-map views and the original Parks Canada river-guide map were acquired and inspected. Together they provide readable geographic coverage across the full selection, establish the two named component corridors, and expose unresolved actual route correspondence in the southern elbow and the northern transfer between separate river valleys. Full selected-route correspondence is therefore not completed. Missing connections are not treated as ordinary name gaps or harmless meander simplification.

records.supported_name_scope: Readable original federal mapping directly supports Silva Creek at the selected headward approach, San Vicente Arroyo below Silver City and Mimbres River along the receiving Deming corridor. Independent INEGI cartography directly labels the terminal plain El Barreal. No continuous natural named river is established along the long intervening desert-plain extension, and its unknown channel or connector names remain null.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selection begins northwest of Silver City on Silva Creek, takes the town corridor below the Pinos Altos Creek junction, then follows San Vicente Arroyo southeast past Silver Acres, the Rio de Arenas junction and the Cameron Creek/Oak Grove Creek surroundings. It continues toward the Mimbres receiving corridor northwest of Deming and passes north of the city before crossing the Interstate 10/US 70 corridor near the airport area. Farther east, the modeled route leaves the visibly mapped river, crosses the developed road-grid and desert plain east of the Florida Mountains and then turns south. It crosses State Highway 9 and the international boundary west of Coyote Hill and Camel Mountain. In Chihuahua it passes west of Cerro El Venado, crosses the plains east of Cerro La Rosina and near San Martín/Nuevo Cuauhtémoc, continues east of Sierra El Máurico and El Mezquite, and ends within the mapped El Barreal plain east of La Morita. It does not follow the upper Mimbres valley, Río Bravo, Casas Grandes–Guzmán or Santa María lake corridors.
records.region: Southwestern New Mexico, United States, and northern Chihuahua, Mexico: Silver City, Deming, the eastern Luna County desert plain and the El Barreal lacustrine plain.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and name-scope review of the entire actual selected route against three original USGS raster exports and the original INEGI Ciudad Juárez geological/topographic-base sheet, with overlapping readable crops and separate private orientation overlays. Retained municipal mapping and already-acquired official hydrology prose support the plain setting. No selected interval lacks readable primary-map coverage. The hold concerns unsupported whole-route river identity and natural-channel continuity across the long plain extension, not unavailable source material.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Complete readable primary cartography establishes the creek–arroyo–Mimbres component sequence and locates the full desert/lacustrine extension to El Barreal. It does not establish one continuous named natural river along that long extension. The missing whole-route identity is a feature/name-scope problem rather than a remaining acquisition or map-coverage gap; unknown connector names remain null.

naming_scope_details.representative_receiving_river_identity: Mimbres River, limited to the verified receiving channel in the Deming corridor.
naming_scope_details.named_terminal_setting: El Barreal; a lacustrine/plain identity, not a river-name alias.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Mimbres River uniformly to Silva Creek, San Vicente Arroyo or the long modeled desert/lacustrine extension south of the mapped Deming river.
Do not substitute Pinos Altos Creek, Rio de Arenas, Cameron Creek, Oak Grove Creek or the northeastern upper Mimbres valley for the selected headward route.
Do not turn El Barreal into a river name or treat its regional lacustrine bed as a measured current shoreline.
Do not transfer Río Santa María, Casas Grandes, Laguna de Guzmán, Laguna de Patos, Río del Carmen or Río Bravo names from neighboring basins or broad groundwater relationships.
Do not interpret missing continuous channel symbols as proof of permanent dryness or absence of every episodic flood connection.
No exact hydronym-transition point, complete natural surface connection, Indigenous alias or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 280.582 km figure is the inventory modeled-mainstem length, not an official length of Silva Creek, San Vicente Arroyo or Mimbres River. The generalized selected line can cross road grids, desert flats and lacustrine ground without representing a surveyed thalweg. Local orientation comparisons use printed graticules or service extents solely to read the selected setting; no geometry modification or point-by-point revalidation was performed.
naming_scope_details.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and name-scope review of the entire actual selected route against three original USGS raster exports and the original INEGI Ciudad Juárez geological/topographic-base sheet, with overlapping readable crops and separate private orientation overlays. Retained municipal mapping and already-acquired official hydrology prose support the plain setting. No selected interval lacks readable primary-map coverage. The hold concerns unsupported whole-route river identity and natural-channel continuity across the long plain extension, not unavailable source material.

records.supported_name_scope: Nahlin River is supported after the initial unnamed southern feeder joins the separately mapped Nahlin arm from the east. The main selection then follows Nahlin downstream to the Sheslay junction, Inklin River to the Nakina junction, and Taku River toward its outlet into Taku Inlet. The sole selected tributary is a short lower Nakina River reach. The initial feeder name remains null.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The eastern selected start lies in a small wetland/stream setting west of the southern valley. It runs generally east, turns north and joins Nahlin River from the south. The named Nahlin arm approaching from the east and the separate Megatushon Creek valley to the west are not the selected headward approach. Nahlin is then followed northwest and west, around its northern bend and south toward the Dudidontu junction, then west to the Sheslay junction. The selection continues west as Inklin River, passing the separate Sutlahine approach, then northwest to Nakina River. Below that junction it follows Taku River southwest through its braided valley, passes the Tulsequah junction, crosses the international boundary and reaches the river–inlet transition. The short northern tributary is lower Nakina, not Sloko River or the upper Nakina system.
records.region: Northwestern British Columbia and southeastern Alaska, from the southern Nahlin headwater area through the Inklin and Taku valleys to the head of Taku Inlet.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected unnamed headward feeder, Nahlin–Inklin–Taku route and lower Nakina tributary.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded correspondence of all four mainstem fragments and the sole tributary against three acquired original federal raster exports. The Canadian upstream/tributary overview and eastern enlargement establish the unnamed initial feeder, its actual receiving junction, Nahlin, Inklin and lower Nakina. The USGS western export overlaps the upper Taku and covers its downstream valley, border crossing and terminal setting. Necessary original-image crops and separate local orientation overlays were inspected across the selection. Unknown feeder naming is preserved without treating it as an unresolved route gap. This establishes connected waterway corridors, not exact banks, all channel threads or an official source point. No full inlet transit is implied.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Unnamed wetland/stream feeder running east and then north into Nahlin River from the south; a selected headward segment rather than an official source determination.
naming_scope_details.upper_named_component: Nahlin River downstream of the selected southern feeder junction, through its northwest and westward upper course to the Sheslay junction.
naming_scope_details.intermediate_named_river_component: Inklin River below the Nahlin–Sheslay junction and above its junction with Nakina River.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Taku River below the Nakina–Inklin junction through British Columbia and Alaska to its river–inlet transition.

selected_tributary_components.name: Nakina River
selected_tributary_components.scope: Only the selected short lower reach into the Inklin junction; excludes the upstream Sloko junction and upper Nakina drainage.

naming_scope_details.lake_scope: No named lake passage is established on the selected route. Nearby Gun Lake, Tedideech Lake and King Salmon Lake are separately mapped and not selected; small channel widenings or wetland pools are not assigned lake names.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Taku River–Taku Inlet transition at the inlet head; generalized eastern mouth-margin setting, not an exact channel, bank or shoreline endpoint.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Taku River uniformly to the initial unnamed feeder, Nahlin River, Inklin River or lower Nakina tributary.
Do not call the initial unnamed southern feeder Nahlin River merely because it drains into it. The separately labeled Nahlin arm entering from the east remains unselected upstream of that junction.
Do not substitute Megatushon Creek, Dudidontu River, upper Sheslay, Sutlahine, Sloko or Tulsequah for the selected mainstem.
No official source-point determination, full Taku Inlet traversal, Indigenous alternative name, legal naming date or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 279.684 km modeled mainstem and 287.005 km modeled network describe the selected combined route and short tributary, not official lengths of Taku River or any individual component. The generalized line simplifies wetland headwaters, channel bends, broad braided corridors and the mouth margin. Source pixels establish the connected corridor and named-component sequence; they do not validate every coordinate or authorize geometry modification.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.

geographic_deferrals.reason: Retained feature bounds at 66.56–68.17°N and 179.97–177.11°W place this object on Chukotka west of Alaska. Actual continental order takes priority over the provisional region_8 assignment.
geographic_deferrals.source_basis: Retained original inventory bounding box and selected-route geographic placement; geographic classification only, no naming source acquired.
